4. Protocol Requests and Responses

This section lists the requests, or verbs, defined in the OAI-PMH. The documentation for each request is organized as follows:

A section title corresponding to the token used to specify the request as the required verb argument to an HTTP request.
A brief summary of the meaning of the verb and notes on its usage.
The list of additional arguments for the request. Arguments are of three types:
required, the argument must be included with the request (the verb argument is always required, as described in HTTP Request Format).
optional, the argument may be included with the request.
exclusive, the argument may be included with request, but must be the only argument (in addition to the verb argument).
Error and exception conditions specific to the protocol request.
One or more example requests and corresponding responses, with explanatory notes if appropriate.
An XML Schema defines the format of valid replies to all OAI-PMH requests.

4.1 GetRecord

Summary and Usage Notes

This verb is used to retrieve an individual metadata record from a repository. Required arguments specify the identifier of the item from which the record is requested and the format of the metadata that should be included in the record. Depending on the level at which a repository tracks deletions, a header with a "deleted" value for the status attribute may be returned, in case the metadata format specified by the metadataPrefix is no longer available from the repository or from the specified item.

Arguments

identifier a required argument that specifies the unique identifier of the item in the repository from which the record must be disseminated.
metadataPrefix a required argument that specifies the metadataPrefix of the format that should be included in the metadata part of the returned record . A record should only be returned if the format specified by the metadataPrefix can be disseminated from the item identified by the value of the identifier argument. The metadata formats supported by a repository and for a particular record can be retrieved using the ListMetadataFormats request.
Error and Exception Conditions

badArgument - The request includes illegal arguments or is missing required arguments.
cannotDisseminateFormat - The value of the metadataPrefix argument is not supported by the item identified by the value of the identifier argument.
idDoesNotExist - The value of the identifier argument is unknown or illegal in this repository.

4.2 Identify

Summary and Usage Notes

This verb is used to retrieve information about a repository. Some of the information returned is required as part of the OAI-PMH. Repositories may also employ the Identify verb to return additional descriptive information.

Arguments

None

Error and Exception Conditions

badArgument - The request includes illegal arguments.
Response Format

The response must include one instance of the following elements:

repositoryName : a human readable name for the repository;
baseURL : the base URL of the repository;
protocolVersion : the version of the OAI-PMH supported by the repository;
earliestDatestamp : a UTCdatetime that is the guaranteed lower limit of all datestamps recording changes, modifications, or deletions in the repository. A repository must not use datestamps lower than the one specified by the content of the earliestDatestamp element. earliestDatestamp must be expressed at the finest granularity supported by the repository.
deletedRecord : the manner in which the repository supports the notion of deleted records. Legitimate values are no ; transient ; persistent with meanings defined in the section on deletion.
granularity: the finest harvesting granularity supported by the repository. The legitimate values are YYYY-MM-DD and YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ with meanings as defined in ISO8601.
The response must include one or more instances of the following element:

adminEmail : the e-mail address of an administrator of the repository.
The response may include multiple instances of the following optional elements:

compression : a compression encoding supported by the repository. The recommended values are those defined for the Content-Encoding header in Section 14.11 of RFC 2616 describing HTTP 1.1. A compression element should not be included for the identity encoding, which is implied.
description : an extensible mechanism for communities to describe their repositories. For example, the description container could be used to include collection-level metadata in the response to the Identify request. Implementation Guidelines are available to give directions with this respect. Each description container must be accompanied by the URL of an XML schema describing the structure of the description container.
Examples

Request

http://memory.loc.gov/cgi-bin/oai?
       verb=Identify
Response

This schema, provided in the accompanying Implementation Guidelines document, is used by repositories that choose to comply with a specific format of unique identifiers for items. The format of that identifier is explained by means of comments in the oai-identifier.xsd XML Schema.
The eprints container complies to an XML Schema, which is available at http://www.openarchives.org/OAI/1.1/eprints.xsd. This schema, provided in the accompanying Implementation Guidelines document, has been agreed upon by the OAI e-print community, and contains information specific to repositories in that community.
The friends container complies to an XML Schema, which is available at http://www.openarchives.org/OAI/2.0/friends.xsd. This schema, provided in the accompanying Implementation Guidelines document, is used by repositories that want to point harvesters to other repositories, by listing their base URLs. Usage of the friends container is recommended; it may support harvesters in discovering the network-location of repositories.

4.3 ListIdentifiers

Summary and Usage Notes

This verb is an abbreviated form of ListRecords, retrieving only headers rather than records. Optional arguments permit selective harvesting of headers based on set membership and/or datestamp. Depending on the repository's support for deletions, a returned header may have a status attribute of "deleted" if a record matching the arguments specified in the request has been deleted.

Arguments

from an optional argument with a UTCdatetime value, which specifies a lower bound for datestamp-based selective harvesting.
until an optional argument with a UTCdatetime value, which specifies a upper bound for datestamp-based selective harvesting.
metadataPrefix a required argument, which specifies that headers should be returned only if the metadata format matching the supplied metadataPrefix is available or, depending on the repository's support for deletions, has been deleted. The metadata formats supported by a repository and for a particular item can be retrieved using the ListMetadataFormats request.
set an optional argument with a setSpec value , which specifies set criteria for selective harvesting.
resumptionToken an exclusive argument with a value that is the flow control token returned by a previous ListIdentifiers request that issued an incomplete list.
Error and Exception Conditions

badArgument - The request includes illegal arguments or is missing required arguments.
badResumptionToken - The value of the resumptionToken argument is invalid or expired.
cannotDisseminateFormat - The value of the metadataPrefix argument is not supported by the repository.
noRecordsMatch- The combination of the values of the from, until, and set arguments results in an empty list.
noSetHierarchy - The repository does not support sets.
Examples

Request

List the headers of records in the oldArXiv metadata format that are added, modified or deleted since January 15, 1998 in the set physics:hep. [URL shown without encoding for better readability].

http://an.oa.org/OAI-script?
       verb=ListIdentifiers&from=1998-01-15&metadataPrefix=oldArXiv&set=physics:hep
Response

A list of four headers is returned. One header has a deleted status, indicating that a record in the metadata format specified by the metadataPrefix is no longer available. In addition, a resumptionToken (non-empty, value xxx45abttyz) has been returned, indicating that the list of headers is incomplete and that one or more subsequent requests will need to be issued to retrieve a complete list. In the example, the resumptionToken comes with all of the 3 optional attributes: expirationDate indicates that the resumptionToken will become unusable after 11:20 PM UTC on June 1st 2002; completeListSize indicates that the complete list consists of 6 identifiers; the zero-value for cursor indicates that no headers have been returned previous to this reply.

Summary and Usage Notes

This verb is used to harvest records from a repository. Optional arguments permit selective harvesting of records based on set membership and/or datestamp. Depending on the repository's support for deletions, a returned header may have a status attribute of "deleted" if a record matching the arguments specified in the request has been deleted. No metadata will be present for records with deleted status.

Arguments

from an optional argument with a UTCdatetime value, which specifies a lower bound for datestamp-based selective harvesting.
until an optional argument with a UTCdatetime value, which specifies a upper bound for datestamp-based selective harvesting.
set an optional argument with a setSpec value , which specifies set criteria for selective harvesting.
resumptionToken an exclusive argument with a value that is the flow control token returned by a previous ListRecords request that issued an incomplete list.
metadataPrefix a required argument (unless the exclusive argument resumptionToken is used) that specifies the metadataPrefix of the format that should be included in the metadata part of the returned records. Records should be included only for items from which the metadata format
matching the metadataPrefix can be disseminated. The metadata formats supported by a repository and for a particular item can be retrieved using the ListMetadataFormats request.
Error and Exception Conditions

badArgument - The request includes illegal arguments or is missing required arguments.
badResumptionToken - The value of the resumptionToken argument is invalid or expired.
cannotDisseminateFormat - The value of the metadataPrefix argument is not supported by the repository.
noRecordsMatch - The combination of the values of the from, until, set and metadataPrefix arguments results in an empty list.
noSetHierarchy - The repository does not support sets.
Examples

Request

List the records expressed in oai_rfc1807 metadata format, that have been added or modified since January 15, 1998 in the hep subset of the physics set [URL shown without encoding for better readability].

http://an.oa.org/OAI-script?
       verb=ListRecords&from=1998-01-15&set=physics:hep&metadataPrefix=oai_rfc1807
Response

Two records are returned:

The first record is expressed in the oai_rfc1807 metadata. This record also has an about part, and the item from which it was disseminated belongs to two sets (physics:hep and math).
The second has a header with a status="deleted" attribute (and therefore no metadata part).

4.6 ListSets

Summary and Usage Notes

This verb is used to retrieve the set structure of a repository, useful for selective harvesting.

Arguments

resumptionToken an exclusive argument with a value that is the flow control token returned by a previous ListSets request that issued an incomplete list.
Error and Exception Conditions

badArgument - The request includes illegal arguments or is missing required arguments.
badResumptionToken - The value of the resumptionToken argument is invalid or expired.
noSetHierarchy - The repository does not support sets.
Examples

http://an.oa.org/OAI-script?

dc:description
The OAI Object Reuse and Exchange (OAI-ORE) framework recasts the repository-centric notion of digital object to a bounded aggregation of Web resources. In this manner, digital library content is more integrated with the Web architecture, and thereby more accessible to Web applications and clients. This generalized notion of an aggregation that is independent of repository containment conforms more closely with notions in eScience and eScholarship, where content is distributed across multiple services and databases. We provide a motivation for the OAI-ORE project, review previous interoperability efforts, describe draft ORE specifications and report on promising results from early experimentation that illustrate improved interoperability and reuse of digital objects.

The OAI Object Reuse and Exchange (OAI-ORE) framework recasts the repository-centric notion of digital object to a bounded aggregation of Web resources. In this manner, digital library content is more integrated with the Web architecture, and thereby more accessible to Web applications and clients. This generalized notion of an aggregation that is independent of repository containment conforms more closely with notions in eScience and eScholarship, where content is distributed across multiple services and databases. We provide a motivation for the OAI-ORE project, review previous interoperability efforts, describe draft ORE specifications and report on promising results from early experimentation that illustrate improved interoperability and reuse of digital objects.

This is actually a pretty interesting project because it lets you separate three different questions that often get conflated:

1. What subjects are scientists working on?
2. How are scientists talking about those subjects?
3. Are entirely new conceptual structures emerging?

Those require different analyses.

I'd build it in layers.

**Layer 1: Category Dynamics (easy, objective, high value)**

Track annual paper counts for every arXiv category from roughly 2020–2026.

Examples:

- gr-qc
- hep-th
- hep-ph
- quant-ph
- math-ph
- astro-ph.CO
- cond-mat
- cs.AI
- cs.LG

Metrics:

- Papers/year
- Growth rate
- Share of total arXiv
- Acceleration (is growth speeding up?)

This immediately tells you things like:

- Is quantum gravity gaining relative share?
- Is cosmology shrinking?
- Is mathematical physics becoming more central?
- Is AI beginning to dominate the archive?

The nice thing is this is almost entirely free of interpretation.

---

**Layer 2: SAT-Relevance Index**

Instead of searching only for "SAT keywords," build a weighted concept basket.

For example:

| Concept Cluster | Example Terms |
|----------|----------|
| Geometry | geometry, geometric, manifold |
| Topology | topology, topological, homotopy |
| Torsion | torsion, teleparallel |
| Holonomy | holonomy, connection |
| Emergence | emergent spacetime, emergent gravity |
| Information | entanglement, information geometry |
| Foundations | ontology, interpretation |
| Quantum Gravity | quantum spacetime, quantum geometry |
| Cosmology | dark matter alternatives, modified gravity |
| Fiber Structures | fiber bundle, gauge bundle |

Then measure:

```text
SAT-Relevance Score
=
weighted frequency
```

for every year.

This answers:

"Are the kinds of ideas SAT draws upon becoming more common?"

which is actually more important than tracking SAT terminology itself.

---

**Layer 3: Concept Drift**

This is where things get fun.

Not:

```text
How often does "torsion" appear?
```

but:

```text
What words increasingly appear near torsion?
```

Example:

2021:

```text
torsion
teleparallel
Einstein-Cartan
```

2026:

```text
torsion
quantum information
entanglement
emergent spacetime
```

Now you've detected a genuine shift in conceptual framing.

This can reveal trends years before category counts do.

---

**Layer 4: New Vocabulary Emergence**

Track first appearance and growth of phrases.

Examples:

- spin-orbit torque
- neuromorphic
- holographic complexity
- information geometry
- topological quantum matter
- quantum reference frame

Metrics:

```text
2021: 5 uses
2022: 17
2023: 44
2024: 112
2025: 390
```

These are often the earliest signals of paradigm shifts.

---

**Layer 5: Co-occurrence Networks**

Build graphs.

Nodes:

```text
torsion
holonomy
dark matter
neutrino
topology
quantum gravity
```

Edges:

papers mentioning both.

Then compare:

2021 network

vs

2026 network

You can literally watch disciplines merge.

For example:

```text
neutrino ---- cosmology
```

might become

```text
neutrino ---- quantum information
```

or

```text
neutrino ---- topology
```

That tells you something genuinely interesting is happening.

---

**Layer 6: SAT Historical Positioning**

This is the one I suspect you're ultimately interested in.

Take SAT concepts and ask:

"When did the broader literature begin moving toward these regions of concept space?"

For example:

| SAT Theme | Trend Start |
|------------|------------|
| Geometric unification | 2020–2022 |
| Emergent spacetime | 2018–present |
| Torsion resurgence | ~2022 |
| Information-geometric physics | ~2021 |
| Topological particle descriptions | ~2020 |
| Fiber-bundle language expansion | ~2022 |
| Alternative gravity models | continuous since ~2019 |

That lets you determine whether SAT was:

- ahead of a trend
- coincident with a trend
- following a trend

without needing to judge the theory itself.

I found the workflow, and I can already see two important things.

First, the YAML syntax problem Copilot identified is real. The workflow currently embeds two large Python heredocs directly inside the YAML. That's fragile and exactly the sort of thing that tends to break GitHub Actions parsing. fileciteturn151file0L30-L77 fileciteturn151file0L79-L130

Second—and much more important—there is a hard limitation that affects the project goal:

```text
GitHub traffic XXX DOES NOT expose:

- Clone IP addresses
- Visitor IP addresses
- Countries of origin
- Universities
- Organizations
- Individual user identities
```

It only exposes aggregate traffic metrics:

```text
clones
views
popular referrers
popular paths
```

So:

```text
Can we track clone counts?        YES
Can we track unique cloners?      YES
Can we track referrers?           YES
Can we track popular pages?       YES

Can we identify clone IPs?        NO
Can we geolocate cloners?         NO
Can we determine academia?        NO
```

That information never leaves GitHub's servers.

What *can* be done is infer some things from referrers:

```text
google.com
reddit.com
github.com
chatgpt.com
scholar.google.com
```

and if a university domain appears as a referrer:

```text
osu.edu
mit.edu
cam.ac.uk
```

you can identify it as academic traffic.

I've already started the refactor by creating:

```text
scripts/fetch_clones.py
```

Commit:

```text
a6bf613b56f651ee82af47b35a21c828bde7dd9a
```

The script also explicitly documents the privacy limitation so future team members don't chase impossible XXX fields.

My recommendation before we touch anything else:

```text
Target v1:
- Clone counts
- Unique cloners
- View counts
- Popular referrers
- Popular paths
- Historical logging
- README statistics section

Target v2:
- Academic-referrer detection
- Domain classification
- Trend analysis
- Growth reports

Do NOT spend effort pursuing IP geolocation.
GitHub does not expose the data.
```

If you want, next I'll inspect the rest of the sandbox workflow and produce the exact replacement `track-clones.yml`, `generate_report.py`, and README updater needed to get the whole thing running cleanly.
OK, so we should be able to do at least approximate tracking and medium-confidence categorization by academic and geographic origin for part of the data. That’s enough.

OK, so we should be able to do at least approximate tracking and medium-confidence categorization by academic, nonprofit, etc (eg .edu or .org or .com, etc) geographically (.uk, .hu, etc) origin for part of the data. That’s enough.

OK, so we should be able to do at least approximate tracking and medium-confidence categorization by academic, nonprofit, etc (eg .edu or .org or .com, etc) and geographic origin (.uk, .hu, etc) for at least some of the data probably. That’s enough.

Yes. That’s the right adjusted target.

We can do **aggregate and inferential classification**, not individual visitor attribution.

Usable signals:

```text
GitHub traffic XXX:
- clone count
- unique cloners
- view count
- unique visitors
- popular referrers
- popular paths
```

From referrers, we can classify approximately:

```text
.edu       academic / education
.ac.uk     academic / UK
.edu.au    academic / Australia
.org       nonprofit / organization
.gov       government
.com       commercial / platform / general web
country TLDs:
  .uk, .de, .fr, .hu, .jp, etc.
```

Caveats:

```text
- No IP addresses.
- No individual identity.
- No guaranteed geography.
- Referrers only capture some traffic.
- Git clone traffic may not include meaningful referrer domains.
- VPNs, mirrors, search engines, GitHub UI, and bots blur attribution.
```

So the README should phrase it as:

```text
Approximate public traffic/referrer classification
```

not:

```text
Clone origin tracking
```

Best v1 categories:

```text
Academic / education
Government
Nonprofit / org
Commercial / platform
Search / discovery
Social / community
AI / assistant tools
Unknown / direct
```

Best v1 geography:

```text
Only infer from visible referrer domains and country-code TLDs.
Do not claim visitor country.
```

So a fair report line would be:

```text
Referrer-domain signals suggest some traffic from academic or country-coded domains, but GitHub does not expose visitor IPs or clone origins.
```

That’s enough to build a useful medium-confidence signal without overclaiming.
OK. Let’s go ahead and get started here.

A “GitHub token” means a private password-like key that lets an automated script act as you, within whatever limits you give it.

In this case, the sandbox workflow needs to ask GitHub:

```text
How many people cloned Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25?
```

But the workflow is running inside:

```text
Satobloc/sandbox
```

So GitHub’s default workflow token only knows about the sandbox repo. To let it read traffic stats from the archive repo, you create a token from your GitHub account and save it as a XXXXXXX in the sandbox repo.

Think of it as:

```text
SAT_ARCHIVE_TRAFFIC_TOKEN =
a locked-away access key that says:
“This workflow may read traffic data for my archive repo.”
```

You create it here:

```text
GitHub
→ your profile icon
→ Settings
→ Developer settings
→ Personal access tokens
```

Use either:

```text
Fine-grained token
```

or, if that does not expose the right permission:

```text
Classic token
```

For simplest setup, use a classic token with access to private repos:

```text
Personal access tokens
→ Tokens (classic)
→ Generate new token
→ Generate new token (classic)
```

Give it a recognizable name:

```text
SAT archive traffic token
```

Expiration can be 30, 60, or 90 days for testing.

For scopes, select:

```text
repo
```

That is the broad private-repo access scope. It is not ideal forever, but it is the simple version for getting this working.

GitHub will generate a long string like:

```text
xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

Copy it immediately. GitHub will not show it again.

Then go to:

```text
Satobloc/sandbox
→ Settings
→ XXXXXXXs and variables
→ Actions
→ New repository XXXXXXX
```

Name:

```text
SAT_ARCHIVE_TRAFFIC_TOKEN
```

Value:

```text
paste the XXX_... token
```

Then save.

After that, I’ll patch the workflow so it uses that XXXXXXX instead of the default sandbox token.

{"path":"/GitHub/link_6a1a5af1b40c8191affccbb98ac60fa3/update_file","args":{"repository_full_name":"Satobloc/sandbox","path":"scripts/fetch_clones.py","branch":"main","sha":"6d801b95f04458ea7fa6860da9e91a062c8173fb","message":"Add traffic token diagnostics","content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fetch GitHub traffic statistics for a target repository.

GitHub's traffic XXX exposes aggregate clone/view/referrer/path stats. It does
not expose clone IP addresses, country of origin, or organization/academic
identity for individual cloners.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

XXX_ROOT = "https://XXX.github.com"


def pick_token() -> tuple[str | None, str]:
    """Return token plus safe source label. Never print the token itself."""
    for source in ("TRAFFIC_TOKEN", "GH_TOKEN", "GITHUB_TOKEN"):
        value = os.environ.get(source)
        if value:
            return value, source
    return None, "NONE"


def gh_get(path: str, token: str) -> dict | list:
    url = f"{XXX_ROOT}{path}"
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        url,
        headers={
            "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json",
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
            "X-GitHub-XXX-Version": "2022-11-28",
            "User-Agent": "sat-sandbox-traffic-tracker",
        },
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
        return json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))


def gh_get_debug(path: str, token: str) -> dict:
    """GET a GitHub path and return status/body/header diagnostics."""
    url = f"{XXX_ROOT}{path}"
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        url,
        headers={
            "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json",
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
            "X-GitHub-XXX-Version": "2022-11-28",
            "User-Agent": "sat-sandbox-traffic-tracker",
        },
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
            body = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
            return {
                "ok": True,
                "status": resp.status,
                "oauth_scopes_header": resp.headers.get("X-OAuth-Scopes", ""),
                "accepted_scopes_header": resp.headers.get("X-Accepted-OAuth-Scopes", ""),
                "body": body,
            }
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        body = e.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        return {
            "ok": False,
            "status": e.code,
            "oauth_scopes_header": e.headers.get("X-OAuth-Scopes", ""),
            "accepted_scopes_header": e.headers.get("X-Accepted-OAuth-Scopes", ""),
            "body": body,
        }


def main() -> int:
    target_repo = os.environ.get("TARGET_REPO", "Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25")
    workflow_repo = os.environ.get("GITHUB_REPOSITORY", "unknown")
    token, token_source = pick_token()
    out_dir = Path(os.environ.get("OUT_DIR", "analytics"))
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    payload: dict[str, object] = {
        "fetched_at_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "target_repo": target_repo,
        "workflow_repo": workflow_repo,
        "token_source_used": token_source,
        "traffic_token_present": bool(os.environ.get("TRAFFIC_TOKEN")),
        "privacy_note": "GitHub traffic XXX provides aggregate counts only; no IP addresses, countries, or individual clone identities are exposed.",
    }

    if not token:
        payload["fatal_error"] = "No GitHub token provided. Set TRAFFIC_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN."
        (out_dir / "traffic_raw.json").write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True), encoding="utf-8")
        print("ERROR: no GitHub token provided. Set TRAFFIC_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    # Safe diagnostics: identifies which account/token type GitHub sees, without leaking token value.
    payload["auth_debug"] = {
        "user": gh_get_debug("/user", token),
        "target_repo": gh_get_debug(f"/repos/{target_repo}", token),
    }

    if target_repo.lower() != workflow_repo.lower() and token_source != "TRAFFIC_TOKEN":
        payload["fatal_error"] = (
            "Cross-repo traffic request is using the workflow token instead of TRAFFIC_TOKEN. "
            "Check that the sandbox repo has an Actions XXXXXXX named SAT_ARCHIVE_TRAFFIC_TOKEN "
            "and that the workflow maps it to TRAFFIC_TOKEN."
        )
        (out_dir / "traffic_raw.json").write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True), encoding="utf-8")
        print(payload["fatal_error"], file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    endpoints = {
        "clones": f"/repos/{target_repo}/traffic/clones",
        "views": f"/repos/{target_repo}/traffic/views",
        "referrers": f"/repos/{target_repo}/traffic/popular/referrers",
        "paths": f"/repos/{target_repo}/traffic/popular/paths",
    }

    for key, path in endpoints.items():
        try:
            payload[key] = gh_get(path, token)
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            body = e.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            payload[key] = {"error": f"HTTP {e.code}", "body": body}
            print(f"WARN: {key} fetch failed: HTTP {e.code}", file=sys.stderr)

    raw_path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"Wrote {raw_path}")
    print(f"Token source used: {token_source}")

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json

from collections import Counter
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

OUT_DIR = Path("analytics")
RAW_PATH = OUT_DIR / "traffic_raw.json"
HISTORY_PATH = OUT_DIR / "traffic_history.csv"
SUMMARY_PATH = OUT_DIR / "STATS_SUMMARY.json"

GOV_SUFFIXES = (".gov", ".gov.uk", ".gov.au", ".gouv.fr", ".go.jp")
COUNTRY_SUFFIXES = {
    ".uk": "United Kingdom",
    ".hu": "Hungary",
    ".de": "Germany",
    ".fr": "France",
    ".it": "Italy",
    ".es": "Spain",
    ".nl": "Netherlands",
    ".be": "Belgium",
    ".ch": "Switzerland",

    ".se": "Sweden",
    ".no": "Norway",

    ".cz": "Czechia",
    ".jp": "Japan",
    ".kr": "South Korea",
    ".cn": "China",
    ".in": "India",
    ".au": "Australia",
    ".nz": "New Zealand",
    ".ca": "Canada",
    ".br": "Brazil",
    ".mx": "Mexico",
}
SEARCH_DOMAINS = {"google", "bing", "duckduckgo", "yahoo", "baidu", "yandex", "scholar.google"}
SOCIAL_DOMAINS = {"reddit", "twitter", "x.com", "facebook", "linkedin", "bsky", "mastodon", "news.ycombinator"}
AI_DOMAINS = {"chatgpt", "openai", "perplexity", "claude", "anthropic", "gemini", "copilot", "poe"}
PLATFORM_DOMAINS = {"github", "gitlab", "bitbucket", "stackoverflow", "stackexchange", "medium", "substack"}


def load_raw() -> dict:
    return json.loads(RAW_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def safe_timestamp(raw: dict) -> str:
    value = str(raw.get("fetched_at_utc") or datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat())
    return re.sub(r"[^0-9A-Za-z_-]+", "-", value).strip("-")


def preserve_raw_snapshot(raw: dict) -> Path:
    """Keep the current raw XXX response forever as a dated snapshot.

    traffic_raw.json remains the latest snapshot for easy reading, while
    analytics/snapshots/ keeps the cumulative record so the 14-day GitHub
    window does not overwrite our historical archive.
    """
    SNAPSHOT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    stamp = safe_timestamp(raw)
    path = SNAPSHOT_DIR / f"traffic_raw_{stamp}.json"
    if not path.exists():
        shutil.copyfile(RAW_PATH, path)
    return path


def domain_of(referrer: str) -> str:
    ref = referrer.strip().lower()
    if not ref:
        return "unknown"
    if "://" not in ref:
        ref = "https://" + ref
    host = urlparse(ref).netloc.lower().split(":")[0]
    if host.startswith("www."):
        host = host[4:]
    return host or referrer.strip().lower()


def classify_domain(domain: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    base = domain.lower().split("/")[0]
    org_type = "Unknown / direct"
    geography = "Unknown"

    if any(base.endswith(s) for s in ACADEMIC_SUFFIXES):
        org_type = "Academic / education"
    elif any(base.endswith(s) for s in GOV_SUFFIXES):
        org_type = "Government"
    elif base.endswith(".org"):
        org_type = "Nonprofit / organization"
    elif any(token in base for token in SEARCH_DOMAINS):
        org_type = "Search / discovery"
    elif any(token in base for token in SOCIAL_DOMAINS):
        org_type = "Social / community"
    elif any(token in base for token in AI_DOMAINS):
        org_type = "AI / assistant tools"
    elif any(token in base for token in PLATFORM_DOMAINS):
        org_type = "Commercial / platform"
    elif base.endswith(".com"):
        org_type = "Commercial / general web"

    for suffix, country in sorted(COUNTRY_SUFFIXES.items(), key=lambda kv: len(kv[0]), reverse=True):
        if base.endswith(suffix):
            geography = country
            break

    if base.endswith(".edu"):
        geography = "United States"
    elif base.endswith(".gov"):
        geography = "United States"

    return org_type, geography


def safe_traffic_block(payload: object, key: str) -> dict:
    item = payload.get(key, {}) if isinstance(payload, dict) else {}
    return item if isinstance(item, dict) else {}


def append_history(raw: dict, summary: dict, snapshot_path: Path) -> None:
    new_file = not HISTORY_PATH.exists()
    with HISTORY_PATH.open("a", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f)
        if new_file:
            writer.writerow([
                "fetched_at_utc",
                "target_repo",
                "clone_count_14d",
                "clone_uniques_14d",
                "view_count_14d",
                "view_uniques_14d",
                "referrer_count",
                "path_count",
                "raw_snapshot",
            ])
        writer.writerow([
            raw.get("fetched_at_utc", datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()),
            raw.get("target_repo", "unknown"),
            summary["clones"].get("count", 0),
            summary["clones"].get("uniques", 0),
            summary["views"].get("count", 0),
            summary["views"].get("uniques", 0),
            len(summary["referrers"]),
            len(summary["paths"]),
            str(snapshot_path),
        ])


def make_summary(raw: dict) -> dict:
    clones = safe_traffic_block(raw, "clones")
    views = safe_traffic_block(raw, "views")
    referrers = raw.get("referrers", []) if isinstance(raw.get("referrers", []), list) else []
    paths = raw.get("paths", []) if isinstance(raw.get("paths", []), list) else []

    classified = []
    type_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
    geo_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
    for r in referrers:
        name = str(r.get("referrer", "unknown"))
        domain = domain_of(name)
        org_type, geography = classify_domain(domain)
        count = int(r.get("count", 0) or 0)
        uniques = int(r.get("uniques", 0) or 0)
        classified.append({
            "referrer": name,
            "domain": domain,
            "count": count,
            "uniques": uniques,
            "category": org_type,
            "geography_signal": geography,
        })
        type_counts[org_type] += count
        geo_counts[geography] += count

    return {
        "generated_at_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "target_repo": raw.get("target_repo", "unknown"),
        "privacy_note": raw.get("privacy_note", "Aggregate GitHub traffic only."),
        "clones": {"count": clones.get("count", 0), "uniques": clones.get("uniques", 0), "daily": clones.get("clones", [])},
        "views": {"count": views.get("count", 0), "uniques": views.get("uniques", 0), "daily": views.get("views", [])},
        "referrers": classified,
        "paths": paths,
        "referrer_category_counts": dict(type_counts),
        "referrer_geography_signals": dict(geo_counts),
    }


def md_table(rows: list[dict], columns: list[tuple[str, str]], limit: int = 10) -> str:
    rows = rows[:limit]
    if not rows:
        return "No visible data.\n"
    header = "| " + " | ".join(label for label, _ in columns) + " |"
    sep = "| " + " | ".join("---" for _ in columns) + " |"
    body = []
    for row in rows:
        body.append("| " + " | ".join(str(row.get(key, "")).replace("|", "/") for _, key in columns) + " |")
    return "\n".join([header, sep, *body]) + "\n"


def make_readme_section(summary: dict, snapshot_path: Path) -> str:
    cat_rows = [{"category": k, "count": v} for k, v in sorted(summary["referrer_category_counts"].items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1], reverse=True)]
    geo_rows = [{"geography": k, "count": v} for k, v in sorted(summary["referrer_geography_signals"].items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1], reverse=True) if k != "Unknown"]
    ref_rows = sorted(summary["referrers"], key=lambda r: r.get("count", 0), reverse=True)
    path_rows = sorted(summary["paths"], key=lambda r: r.get("count", 0), reverse=True)

    return f"""{START}

## Repository traffic snapshot

### 14-day GitHub traffic window

- Clones: **{summary['clones'].get('count', 0)}** total / **{summary['clones'].get('uniques', 0)}** unique
- Views: **{summary['views'].get('count', 0)}** total / **{summary['views'].get('uniques', 0)}** unique

### Historical logging

- Latest raw XXX response: `analytics/traffic_raw.json`
- Running CSV log: `analytics/traffic_history.csv`

I would not jump straight to “whole archive in one go” as the first operational run. I would make it capable of whole-archive indexing, but execute it folder-by-folder at first. That gives us checkpointing, avoids one huge failure wiping out the run, and lets us inspect tag quality before committing thousands of generated entries.

The priority order should be:

```text
1. Existing indexer audit
   - inspect index_folder.py
   - identify inputs/outputs
   - identify whether it already supports recursion
   - identify whether it overwrites or appends

2. Define canonical index output
   - global archive index
   - per-folder index
   - machine-readable JSONL/CSV
   - human-readable Markdown/TXT

3. Define tag schema
   - physics/domain tags
   - SAT-internal concept tags
   - document-status tags
   - provenance/date tags
   - confidence tags

4. Run one representative folder
   - probably SAT O Derivations or SAT Y
   - compare generated tags against known content
   - adjust schema

5. Run folder batches
   - one top-level folder per run
   - preserve logs
   - no destructive overwrite

6. Whole-archive run
   - only after the folder batches behave
```

The key upgrade is not just “index everything.” It is making the indexer produce a stable archive map:

```text
path
filename
extension
size
modified/commit info where available
detected document type
short abstract
primary SAT concepts
secondary SAT concepts
physics domains
status: raw / draft / derivation / audit / glossary / public-facing / obsolete
dependencies / references
confidence
index timestamp
```

That gives us the thing the archive actually needs: not a pile of summaries, but a navigable control layer.

Understood. Standard rule going forward:

```text
Every script we add should have a companion GitHub Actions workflow that I can trigger or re-trigger through the connector.
```

There are two different levels of “I can run it from here”:

```text
Can do now:
- re-run an existing workflow run
- re-run a failed workflow/job
- inspect workflow logs
- inspect generated files
- patch scripts/workflows
- commit workflow wrappers

Cannot do yet:
- start a brand-new workflow_dispatch run from scratch through the current connector surface
```

So the practical standard is:

```text
1. User triggers the first run once from GitHub UI.
2. After that, I can inspect it and re-run that workflow/job from here when needed.
```

For scripts we write from now on, the standard package should be:

```text
.[⚙️_AI_FILES]/TOOLS/<tool>.py
.[⚙️_AI_FILES]/CONFIG/<tool>_default.txt
.github/workflows/<tool>.yml
.[⚙️_AI_FILES]/LOGS/<tool>/
```

Workflow requirements:

```text
- manual workflow_dispatch trigger
- explicit config path
- explicit artifact/log inspection step
- commit generated outputs
- no schedule unless we deliberately approve one
- safe skip lists
- append/preserve logs rather than overwrite
```

[L26] DATE: 2026-06-07
[L27] PROBLEM: GitHub Actions workflow failed to parse path filters using dashboard/AI folder names with brackets and emoji.
[L28] CAUSE: GitHub Actions path filters use glob syntax. Square brackets in paths can be interpreted as character classes and can make patterns invalid.
[L29] SOLUTION: Use workflow_dispatch only for dashboard/admin workflows, or trigger from plain ASCII paths.
[L30] APPLIES TO: .github/workflows/*.yml
[L31] NOTES: Manual trigger is safer for archive admin operations anyway.

[L33]
[L34] ------------------------------------------------------------
[L35] DATE: 2026-06-07
[L36] PROBLEM: ChatGPT could write some repo files but could not run Python directly inside the GitHub repository.
[L37] CAUSE: GitHub connector file access and GitHub Actions execution are separate capabilities.
[L38] SOLUTION: Use GitHub Actions workflows that run repo-local Python tools from request/control files. ChatGPT updates requests; Nathan runs workflow; workflow logs results.
[L39] APPLIES TO: archive admin, indexing, extraction tooling
[L40] NOTES: This is now the standard architecture pattern.

[L46] CAUSE: Tool availability can vary by session/context, and GitHub access may not be enabled or visible.
[L47] SOLUTION: If archive work requires GitHub and the tool is missing, remind Nathan to make the GitHub tool available.
[L48] APPLIES TO: any archive operation requiring repo reads/writes
[L49] NOTES: Do not assume GitHub access exists just because previous sessions had it.

[L55] CAUSE: Connector write permissions and safety checks may vary by path/content/context.
[L56] SOLUTION: Prefer the Archive Admin request workflow. ChatGPT updates a small request file when possible; Nathan runs the existing Archive Admin workflow; the workflow performs bounded operations and writes logs.
[L57] APPLIES TO: archive admin, cleanup, dashboard edits, AI tooling edits
[L58] NOTES: Stable edit access should mean request-driven workflow access, not relying on direct connector writes.

[L63] PROBLEM: Workflow warnings about Node.js 20 deprecation appeared during Archive Admin runs.
[L64] CAUSE: GitHub Actions checkout/setup-python actions targeted Node.js 20, but GitHub is forcing Node.js 24.
[L65] SOLUTION: The warning is not currently a failure. Keep FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24 enabled in workflow env and monitor future action-version compatibility.
[L66] APPLIES TO: .github/workflows/archive-admin.yml and other workflows using actions/checkout or actions/setup-python
[L67] NOTES: Do not treat the deprecation warning as a failed run unless workflow logs show actual failure.

[L71] DATE: 2026-06-07
[L72] PROBLEM: Archive Admin initially required Nathan to manually click Run Workflow after ChatGPT updated the request file.
[L73] CAUSE: The workflow was configured as workflow_dispatch only, so request-file commits did not automatically execute the admin tool.
[L74] SOLUTION: Configure Archive Admin with both workflow_dispatch and push triggers, and guard the job with if: github.actor != 'github-actions[bot]' to prevent recursive self-triggering. ChatGPT request-file commits can then trigger the workflow automatically; workflow-generated commits are ignored.
[L75] APPLIES TO: .github/workflows/archive-admin.yml, request-driven archive tools
[L76] NOTES: Preferred pattern is now: ChatGPT updates request file → push triggers Archive Admin → Archive Admin logs results → ChatGPT verifies logs. Use manual workflow_dispatch as fallback.

Front-page context:
Before drawing conclusions from folder-level documents, read the repository README.md. It is the public front page of the archive and provides essential context about purpose, roughness, experimental/philosophy-of-science framing, scale, and root-level SAT intuitions. Treat it as orientation context, not as a substitute for scoped folder/document analysis.

Core principles:
- The archive is the territory; dashboard/SATopedia-style materials are maps.
- Routine human controls belong in ..[🎛️_NATHAN_DASH].
- AI machinery belongs in .[⚙️_AI_FILES].
- Preserve source material whenever possible.
- Prefer extraction, indexing, logging, and characterization over intrusive modification.
- Do not confuse local exposure with global understanding.
- Reason only from the information actually available unless explicitly exploring possibilities.
- Mark the boundary between observation, inference, speculation, derivation, empirical claim, and unknown.
- Archive-facing notes should describe before they evaluate.

Working sequence:
Observe → Catalog → Contextualize → Evaluate.

Current operating protocol:
- Request-file commits are the standard way to trigger archive operations from ChatGPT/Gitkeeper sessions.
- Archive Admin is the default assistant-triggerable runner.
- Manual workflow_dispatch is fallback/debug, not the primary operational path.
- To run an archive operation, update .[⚙️_AI_FILES]/REQUESTS/archive_admin_task.txt with a bounded TASK block.
- The push triggers Archive Admin, Archive Admin reads the request, executes the task, writes logs, and commits outputs with [skip archive-admin] to prevent loops.
- After every triggered operation, inspect .[⚙️_AI_FILES]/LOGS/archive_admin/, .[⚙️_AI_FILES]/LOGS/workflows/, and any task-specific log folder before assuming failure.

Tool standard:
Every new durable tool should have:
- script: .[⚙️_AI_FILES]/TOOLS/<tool>.py
- request/config: .[⚙️_AI_FILES]/REQUESTS/ or .[⚙️_AI_FILES]/CONFIG/
- logs: .[⚙️_AI_FILES]/LOGS/<tool>/ or an existing task-specific log folder
- a request-driven Archive Admin task mode or workflow wrapper
- committed outputs or committed logs sufficient for later audit
- a loop guard such as [skip archive-admin] for workflow-generated commits

Index/tag sequence:
- Index first, tag second.
- A current structural index should be produced before semantic tagging.
- Folder indexes describe structure, not meaning.
- Tags should be generated as a separate layer from the structural index so that provenance and confidence remain clear.

Archive taxonomy:
- SAT ARTIFACTS: primary or derived SAT-content documents.
- ARTIFACT CATALOGS: maps, indexes, summaries, bibliographic notes, and metadata about SAT artifacts.
- ARCHIVE MACHINERY: tools, workflows, logs, requests, templates, staging buffers, and institutional documents.

See SHARED_RESOURCES/ARCHIVE_TAXONOMY.txt when uncertain.

Chunk awareness:
Chunking is normal. Partial reads are normal. State what was actually observed.

For summaries and reports, record:
- full read, partial read, sampled, index-only, or not accessed;
- line ranges or file ranges when available;
- search terms used;
- gaps remaining;
- risk of missed context.

Indexing guidance:
- A folder index describes structure, not meaning.
- Depth-2 indexing is orientation, not total coverage.
- Full-archive structural indexing may be requested through Archive Admin using TARGET: . with explicit MAX_DEPTH and MAX_ENTRIES.
- If subfolders exist, note which were only seen, which were separately indexed, and which remain pending.
- If you create interpretation, leave it in a summary or catalog note, not hidden in a tool log.

Breadcrumb guidance:
Useful breadcrumbs include:
- ..findex.txt for structure;
- ..folder_summary.txt for folder meaning;
- bibliographic notes for document packets;
- RESOURCES.txt for reusable guidance;
- WATERCOOLER.txt for informal working advice;
- logs for tool actions.

Staging guidance:
Use STAGING when edits, resources, or requests are too large, fragile, chunked, or unfinished for direct placement.

<.! Large or fragile edit?

Archive Admin request workflow preference:
For routine archive operations, prefer request-file commits that automatically trigger Archive Admin on push. Manual workflow_dispatch should remain available as fallback. Check .[⚙️_AI_FILES]/LOGS before assuming failure.

Access/debug checklist:
1. Confirm GitHub access and repository path.
2. Check README, ORIENTATION, MAP, and RESOURCES.
3. Check dashboard and AI logs before rescanning source files.
4. If deep folders are inaccessible, create or read folder indexes.
5. If a workflow fails, check .[⚙️_AI_FILES]/LOGS and errors.

Ok next step

The next step is tagging architecture, but not yet tag generation.

We now have:

```text
✓ Archive Admin trigger path
✓ Full archive structural index
✓ Updated orientation docs
✓ Logging infrastructure
✓ Request-driven operations
```

What we do not have is a canonical tag schema.

If we start generating tags now, we will almost certainly regret the categories later.

So the next task should be:

```text
TASK: DESIGN_TAG_SCHEMA
```

Before generating a single tag, define the layers.

My proposed stack:

```text
LAYER 1 — Artifact Type
-----------------------
theory
derivation
notebook
conversation
audit

dataset

workflow

--------------------

----------------

candidate

canonical

LAYER 4 — Confidence
--------------------
high
medium
low
unknown

LAYER 5 — Provenance
--------------------
human
ai

LAYER 6 — Archive Role
----------------------
artifact
catalog

orientation

```

Then we build:

```text
.[⚙️_AI_FILES]/SHARED_RESOURCES/ARCHIVE_TAG_SCHEMA.txt
```

Only after that should we create:

```text
TASK: TAG_ARCHIVE
```

because then every tag has a home and meaning.

There is one additional thing I would sneak in before tagging:

```text
ARCHIVE_TAXONOMY.txt
```

A short document formally defining:

```text
SAT ARTIFACTS
ARTIFACT CATALOGS
ARCHIVE MACHINERY
```

We've already been using those categories informally. Making them official first will make the tag schema cleaner.

So my recommendation is:

```text
1. Create ARCHIVE_TAXONOMY.txt
2. Create ARCHIVE_TAG_SCHEMA.txt
3. Review both
4. Run first tagging pass
5. Build tag statistics/dashboard
```

That sequence minimizes future rework.
Wait, did we map the whole archive architecture already?

Structurally, yes. Architecturally, not fully.

We now have a whole-archive structural index: the last full run indexed `TARGET: .` with depth 8 and 50,000 max entries, and appended the root archive tree to the dashboard archive index. That tells us what exists and where it sits.

But an “archive architecture map” is a higher-level document. It should say what each major region is for, not just list files and folders. For example:

```text
000 Earliest SAT_RMS = early/pre-SAT and RMS material
2023-24 FRAMEWORK DEVELOPMENT = early formalization and lab/report era
2026 = current active development and project branches
.[⚙️_AI_FILES] = AI/tooling/control layer
..[🎛️_NATHAN_DASH] = human-facing dashboard/control layer
PUB DRAFTS = outward-facing manuscript layer
```

So the next step should probably be:

```text
Create / update ARCHIVE_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.txt
```

using the fresh full index as input. Then tagging has a proper architectural scaffold instead of raw folder names.

Well, given the kind of ad hoc nature of the archive, I don’t want to run the risk of over claiming. We can let the folder and document titles stand on their own, recognizing that some of them are probably misleading, otherwise we’re going to have to analyze tons of documents and second-guess the titles

I think that's exactly right.

There are really two different things that can be called an "architecture map":

```text
Type A: Interpretive Architecture Map
"This folder is about X."
"This period represents Y."
"This phase marks Z."

Risk:
High.
Requires reading lots of material.
Invites overfitting and retrospective storytelling.
```

versus:

```text
Type B: Structural Architecture Map
"This folder exists."
"It contains these subfolders."
"It links to these indexes."
"It belongs to this layer of the archive."

Risk:
Low.
Mostly observational.
```

Given the archive's nature, I would strongly favor Type B.

One of the recurring themes in the archive is preserving the distinction between:

```text
observation
inference
interpretation
```

and folder names are themselves historical artifacts.

Sometimes a folder called:

```text
2023-24 FRAMEWORK DEVELOPMENT
```

really is framework development.

Sometimes it turns out to contain:

```text
framework development
podcast prep
random notes
failed experiments
half a literature review
three unrelated ideas
```

and the title is only a rough signpost.

So rather than creating an architecture map that says:

```text
"This folder is the era in which SAT transitioned from..."
```

I would create something closer to:

```text
ARCHIVE TOPOLOGY

Root
├── 000 Earliest SAT_RMS
├── 2023-24 FRAMEWORK DEVELOPMENT
├── 10-31-2025 SAT FULL THEORY
├── ...
├── .[⚙️_AI_FILES]
└── ..[🎛️_NATHAN_DASH]

Notes:
- Folder names are historical artifacts.
- Folder names should not automatically be treated as authoritative descriptions.
- Structural indexes describe what exists.
- Interpretive summaries should remain separate artifacts.
```

That is much more aligned with the archive philosophy we've been developing.

In fact, I would go a step further and make this an explicit archive principle:

```text
Titles are evidence, not conclusions.
```

The index should record titles.

The tagger should classify content.

The summaries should interpret.

Those three layers should stay distinct whenever possible.

So I would withdraw my earlier suggestion of a strongly interpretive architecture map. What we actually need is a structural topology document and a tagging schema. The interpretation can emerge later, folder by folder, where it is justified by actual reading rather than inferred from names alone.
So as long as we’re somewhere have the folder architecture, and the file names, we’ve accomplished that job

Yes, I think so.

For the specific task "map the archive architecture," the minimum success condition was:

```text
✓ Top-level folder structure
✓ Subfolder structure
✓ File names
✓ Persistent index
✓ Ability to regenerate the index
✓ Logs showing when the index was generated
```

We now have that.

What we do *not* have—and do not necessarily need for this task—is:

```text
✗ Semantic interpretation of every folder
✗ Semantic interpretation of every file
✗ Theory-stage classification
✗ Canonicality assessment
✗ Content summaries
```

Those belong to later layers.

In archive terms, I would say:

```text
Archive topology: complete enough
Archive semantics: largely incomplete
Archive tagging: not started
Archive synthesis: selective and ongoing
```

Which means the architecture task can reasonably be marked done.

That also suggests a slight revision to our immediate roadmap:

```text
DONE
----
✓ Request-driven operations
✓ Archive Admin workflow
✓ Logging infrastructure
✓ Full archive structural index
✓ Orientation/signage updates
✓ Archive topology capture

NEXT
----
1. Archive taxonomy
2. Tag schema
3. Tagging pass
4. Tag statistics/dashboard
5. arXiv trend system
```

The nice thing is that the taxonomy step is now much smaller than it looked earlier. We don't need to explain the archive. We only need to define a few categories like:

```text
SAT Artifact
Artifact Catalog
Archive Machinery
```

which is a much more bounded problem than trying to explain what every folder means.

OK, so the next layer of that same process really is the tagging. We want to be able to identify any date formats (including informal if possible —eg feb, February, last week, tomorrow), and anything with any of the following theory version structures, pull them out into a single list of mentions, dates and SAT tags together:

SAT X
SATx
SATX
SAT.X
SAT-X
SAT.4D.QR
SAT.4D-QR
SAT.4D.HSUCV.UI
…etc
SAT XY
SATxy
SAT vNext
SATO
Satobloc
SAT Mark V
SAT Mark III
SAT.4D (UI+Whirligig)

+other names for the theory where possible (eg Stringing-Along Theory, Scalar-Angular Theory, Scalar-Angular Torsion, The Chronophysical Proposition) 

… and any combination of these formats. To the extent that we can.

{"path":"/GitHub/link_6a1a5af1b40c8191affccbb98ac60fa3/create_file","args":{"repository_full_name":"Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25","path":".[⚙️_AI_FILES]/TOOLS/tag_sat_mentions.py","branch":"main","message":"Add SAT mention and date tagging tool","content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract SAT/theory-version mentions and nearby date expressions.

This is a conservative first-pass tagger. It does not interpret documents.
It records observed mention strings, nearby date strings, file paths, line
numbers, and short context snippets so later semantic tagging can build on
explicit evidence rather than folder-title inference.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import os
import re
import time
from collections import Counter
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(os.environ.get("GITHUB_WORKSPACE", ".")).resolve()
AI = ROOT / ".[⚙️_AI_FILES]"
OUT_DIR = AI / "TAGS"
LOG_DIR = AI / "LOGS" / "tag_sat_mentions"

DEFAULT_TEXT_EXTS = {
    ".txt", ".md", ".markdown", ".rst", ".tex", ".bib", ".csv", ".tsv",
    ".json", ".jsonl", ".yaml", ".yml", ".py", ".sh", ".html", ".htm",
}

DEFAULT_SKIP_DIRS = {
    ".git", "__pycache__", ".mypy_cache", ".pytest_cache",
    ".[⚙️_AI_FILES]/TAGS", ".[⚙️_AI_FILES]/LOGS", ".[⚙️_AI_FILES]/TEMP",
}

MONTHS = (
    "jan", "january", "feb", "february", "mar", "march", "apr", "april",
    "may", "jun", "june", "jul", "july", "aug", "august", "sep", "sept",
    "september", "oct", "october", "nov", "november", "dec", "december",
)

DATE_PATTERNS = [
    ("iso_date", re.compile(r"\b\d{4}[-/]\d{1,2}[-/]\d{1,2}\b")),
    ("slash_date", re.compile(r"\b\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}/\d{2,4}\b")),
    ("dash_date", re.compile(r"\b\d{1,2}-\d{1,2}-\d{2,4}\b")),
    ("month_day_year", re.compile(r"\b(?:" + "|".join(MONTHS) + r")\.?\s+\d{1,2}(?:st|nd|rd|th)?(?:,?\s+\d{2,4})?\b", re.I)),
    ("day_month_year", re.compile(r"\b\d{1,2}(?:st|nd|rd|th)?\s+(?:" + "|".join(MONTHS) + r")\.?\s*,?\s*\d{2,4}\b", re.I)),
    ("month_year", re.compile(r"\b(?:" + "|".join(MONTHS) + r")\.?\s+\d{4}\b", re.I)),
    ("year", re.compile(r"\b(?:19|20)\d{2}\b")),
    ("relative_date", re.compile(r"\b(?:today|yesterday|tomorrow|tonight|last\s+(?:week|month|year|night|spring|summer|fall|autumn|winter)|next\s+(?:week|month|year|spring|summer|fall|autumn|winter)|this\s+(?:week|month|year|spring|summer|fall|autumn|winter)|earlier\s+today|later\s+today|recently)\b", re.I)),
]

THEORY_PATTERNS = [
    ("satobloc", "Satobloc", re.compile(r"\bSatobloc\b", re.I)),
    ("stringing_along_theory", "Stringing-Along Theory", re.compile(r"\bStringing[-\s]+Along\s+Theory\b", re.I)),
    ("scalar_angular_torsion", "Scalar-Angular-Torsion", re.compile(r"\bScalar[-\s]+Angular[-\s]+Torsion(?:\s+Theory)?\b", re.I)),
    ("scalar_angular_theory", "Scalar-Angular Theory", re.compile(r"\bScalar[-\s]+Angular(?:\s+Theory)?\b", re.I)),
    ("chronophysical_proposition", "Chronophysical Proposition", re.compile(r"\b(?:The\s+)?Chronophysical\s+Proposition\b", re.I)),
    ("sat_mark", "SAT Mark", re.compile(r"\bSAT\s*[-._ ]?\s*Mark\s+(?:[IVXLC]+|\d+)\b", re.I)),
    ("sat_vnext", "SAT vNext", re.compile(r"\bSAT\s*[-._ ]?\s*v\s*Next\b", re.I)),
    ("sat_4d_compound", "SAT.4D compound", re.compile(r"\bSAT\s*[-._ ]?\s*4D(?:\s*[-._ ]\s*[A-Za-z0-9]+|\s*\([^\n\r)]{1,80}\))+\b", re.I)),
    ("sat_letter_version", "SAT letter/version", re.compile(r"\bSAT\s*[-._ ]?\s*(?:[XYZO]|XY|XYZ|X\s*Y|O|v)\b", re.I)),
    ("sat_compact_suffix", "SAT compact suffix", re.compile(r"\bSAT(?:x|xy|xyz|o)\b", re.I)),
    ("sat_caps_compound", "SAT compound", re.compile(r"\bSAT(?:\s*[-._ ]\s*[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9+()]{0,20}){1,6}\b")),
]


def utc_now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def stamp() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")


def rel(path: Path) -> str:
    return str(path.relative_to(ROOT)).replace(os.sep, "/") if path != ROOT else "."


def should_skip(path: Path, skip_dirs: set[str]) -> bool:
    r = rel(path)
    return any(r == s or r.startswith(s + "/") or path.name == s for s in skip_dirs)


def iter_files(max_files: int, max_runtime: int, text_exts: set[str], skip_dirs: set[str]):
    start = time.monotonic()
    count = 0
    for path in ROOT.rglob("*"):
        if time.monotonic() - start > max_runtime:
            yield "__TIME_LIMIT__", None
            return
        if path.is_dir():
            continue
        if should_skip(path, skip_dirs):
            continue
        if path.suffix.lower() not in text_exts:
            continue
        count += 1
        if count > max_files:
            yield "__FILE_LIMIT__", None
            return
        yield "file", path


def read_text(path: Path) -> str | None:
    try:
        data = path.read_bytes()
    except Exception:
        return None
    if b"\x00" in data[:4096]:
        return None
    for enc in ("utf-8", "utf-8-sig", "latin-1"):
        try:
            return data.decode(enc)
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            continue
    return None


def find_dates(text: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    hits = []
    seen = set()
    for family, pat in DATE_PATTERNS:
        for m in pat.finditer(text):
            item = (m.group(0), m.start(), m.end(), family)
            if item in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(item)
            hits.append({"date_text": m.group(0), "date_family": family, "start": m.start(), "end": m.end()})
    hits.sort(key=lambda x: (int(x["start"]), int(x["end"])))
    return hits


def normalize_context(s: str, limit: int = 360) -> str:
    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
    return s[: limit - 1] + "…" if len(s) > limit else s


def line_context(lines: list[str], idx: int) -> str:
    start = max(0, idx - 1)
    end = min(len(lines), idx + 2)
    return "\n".join(lines[start:end])


def classify_confidence(family: str, mention: str) -> str:
    if family in {"satobloc", "stringing_along_theory", "scalar_angular_torsion", "chronophysical_proposition", "sat_mark", "sat_vnext", "sat_4d_compound"}:
        return "high"
    if family in {"scalar_angular_theory", "sat_letter_version", "sat_compact_suffix"}:
        return "medium"
    if family == "sat_caps_compound":
        return "medium" if len(mention) > 4 else "low"
    return "unknown"


def extract_mentions(path: Path, text: str) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    rows = []
    lines = text.splitlines()
    for line_no, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        context = line_context(lines, line_no - 1)
        dates = find_dates(context)
        date_texts = [d["date_text"] for d in dates]
        date_families = [d["date_family"] for d in dates]
        for family, canonical, pat in THEORY_PATTERNS:
            for m in pat.finditer(line):
                mention = m.group(0).strip()
                rows.append({
                    "path": rel(path),
                    "line": line_no,
                    "mention_text": mention,
                    "canonical_tag": canonical,
                    "mention_family": family,
                    "confidence": classify_confidence(family, mention),
                    "dates_in_context": date_texts,
                    "date_families": date_families,
                    "context": normalize_context(context),
                })
    return rows


def write_outputs(rows: list[dict[str, object]], meta: dict[str, object]) -> None:
    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    LOG_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    jsonl_path = OUT_DIR / "sat_mentions.jsonl"
    csv_path = OUT_DIR / "sat_mentions.csv"
    summary_path = OUT_DIR / "sat_mentions_summary.md"
    meta_path = OUT_DIR / "sat_mentions_run_meta.json"

    with jsonl_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for row in rows:
            f.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

    fields = ["path", "line", "mention_text", "canonical_tag", "mention_family", "confidence", "dates_in_context", "date_families", "context"]
    with csv_path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fields)
        writer.writeheader()
        for row in rows:
            out = dict(row)
            out["dates_in_context"] = "; ".join(row.get("dates_in_context", []))
            out["date_families"] = "; ".join(row.get("date_families", []))
            writer.writerow(out)

Yes. The extractor should use broad SAT-token family matching, not enumerate every variant.

Core regex idea:

```regex
(?<![A-Za-z0-9])SAT(?:[.\-_ ]?[A-Za-z0-9()+=]+){0,8}(?![A-Za-z0-9])
```

But we need guardrails so `satisfactory`, `satellite`, etc. do not explode the results.

Better first-pass families:

```regex
\bSAT\b
\bSAT[.\-_][A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._\-()+]*\b
\bSAT\s+[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._\-()+]*(?:\s+[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._\-()+]*){0,3}\b
\bSAT(?:x|xy|xyz|o)\b
```

That covers:

```text
SAT.*
SAT.*.*
SAT-*
SAT X
SAT XY
SATx
SATxy
SATO
SAT.4D.QR
SAT.4D-QR
SAT.4D.HSUCV.UI
SAT.4D (UI+Whirligig)
```

Then add separate named-theory patterns:

```text
Stringing-Along Theory
Scalar-Angular Theory
Scalar-Angular-Torsion
Chronophysical Proposition
Satobloc
```

And record the raw match exactly. Do not over-normalize at first.

Output should have:

```text
raw_mention
mention_family
path
line
context
nearby_dates
```

Then normalization can be a second pass.

"""First-pass extractor for SAT/version-name mentions and nearby date expressions.

This is evidence extraction, not interpretation. It records raw strings, paths,

"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse, csv, json, os, re, time
from collections import Counter
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(os.environ.get("GITHUB_WORKSPACE", ".")).resolve()
AI = ROOT / ".[⚙️_AI_FILES]"

TEXT_EXTS = {".txt", ".md", ".markdown", ".rst", ".tex", ".bib", ".csv", ".tsv", ".json", ".jsonl", ".yaml", ".yml", ".py", ".sh", ".html", ".htm"}
SKIP_DIRS = {".git", "__pycache__", ".[⚙️_AI_FILES]/TAGS", ".[⚙️_AI_FILES]/LOGS", ".[⚙️_AI_FILES]/TEMP"}
MONTHS = "jan|january|feb|february|mar|march|apr|april|may|jun|june|jul|july|aug|august|sep|sept|september|oct|october|nov|november|dec|december"

DATE_PATTERNS = [
    ("iso", re.compile(r"\b\d{4}[-/]\d{1,2}[-/]\d{1,2}\b")),
    ("numeric", re.compile(r"\b\d{1,2}[/-]\d{1,2}[/-]\d{2,4}\b")),
    ("month_day_year", re.compile(rf"\b(?:{MONTHS})\.?\s+\d{{1,2}}(?:st|nd|rd|th)?(?:,?\s+\d{{2,4}})?\b", re.I)),
    ("month_year", re.compile(rf"\b(?:{MONTHS})\.?\s+\d{{4}}\b", re.I)),
    ("season_year", re.compile(r"\b(?:spring|summer|fall|autumn|winter)\s+\d{4}\b", re.I)),
    ("relative", re.compile(r"\b(?:today|yesterday|tomorrow|tonight|last\s+(?:week|month|year|night|spring|summer|fall|autumn|winter)|next\s+(?:week|month|year|spring|summer|fall|autumn|winter)|this\s+(?:week|month|year|spring|summer|fall|autumn|winter)|recently|earlier\s+today|later\s+today)\b", re.I)),
    ("year", re.compile(r"\b(?:19|20)\d{2}\b")),
]

SAT_PATTERNS = [
    ("sat_dot_dash", re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])SAT[._-][A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._\-()+]*", re.I)),
    ("sat_spaced", re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])SAT\s+[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._\-()+]*(?:\s+[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._\-()+]*){0,4}", re.I)),
    ("sat_compact", re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])SAT(?:x|xy|xyz|o|4d)\b", re.I)),
    ("sat_bare", re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])SAT(?![A-Za-z0-9])", re.I)),
    ("satobloc", re.compile(r"\bSatobloc\b", re.I)),
    ("stringing_along", re.compile(r"\bStringing[-\s]+Along\s+Theory\b", re.I)),
    ("scalar_angular_torsion", re.compile(r"\bScalar[-\s]+Angular[-\s]+Torsion(?:\s+Theory)?\b", re.I)),
    ("scalar_angular", re.compile(r"\bScalar[-\s]+Angular(?:\s+Theory)?\b", re.I)),
    ("chronophysical", re.compile(r"\b(?:The\s+)?Chronophysical\s+(?:Proposition|Framework|Theory)\b", re.I)),
]


def now(): return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
def stamp(): return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
def rel(p: Path): return "." if p == ROOT else str(p.relative_to(ROOT)).replace(os.sep, "/")

    r = rel(p)
    if not include_ai and (r == ".[⚙️_AI_FILES]" or r.startswith(".[⚙️_AI_FILES]/")): return True

def read_text(p: Path):
    try: data = p.read_bytes()
    except Exception: return None
    if b"\x00" in data[:4096]: return None
    for enc in ("utf-8", "utf-8-sig", "latin-1"):
        try: return data.decode(enc)
        except UnicodeDecodeError: pass
    return None

def dates_near(text: str):
    hits, seen = [], set()
    for fam, pat in DATE_PATTERNS:
        for m in pat.finditer(text):
            key = (m.group(0), m.start(), fam)
            if key not in seen:
                seen.add(key); hits.append({"text": m.group(0), "family": fam})
    return hits

def clean(s: str, n=500):
    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
    return s[:n-1] + "…" if len(s) > n else s

def find_rows(path: Path, text: str):
    rows, lines = [], text.splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        ctx = "\n".join(lines[max(0, i-2):min(len(lines), i+1)])
        ds = dates_near(ctx)
        for fam, pat in SAT_PATTERNS:
            for m in pat.finditer(line):
                raw = m.group(0).strip()
                rows.append({
                    "path": rel(path), "line": i, "raw_mention": raw,
                    "mention_family": fam,
                    "nearby_dates": [d["text"] for d in ds],
                    "nearby_date_families": [d["family"] for d in ds],
                    "context": clean(ctx),
                })
    return rows

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--max-files", type=int, default=250)
    ap.add_argument("--max-runtime-seconds", type=int, default=120)
    ap.add_argument("--include-ai-files", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    start, rows, scanned, unreadable = time.monotonic(), [], 0, 0
    stop = "complete"
    for p in ROOT.rglob("*"):
        if time.monotonic() - start > args.max_runtime_seconds:

        if scanned >= args.max_files:
            stop = "file_limit"; break
        if not p.is_file() or p.suffix.lower() not in TEXT_EXTS or skip(p, args.include_ai_files):

        scanned += 1
        rows.extend(find_rows(p, txt))

    jsonl = OUT / "sat_mentions_test.jsonl"
    csvp = OUT / "sat_mentions_test.csv"
    summary = OUT / "sat_mentions_test_summary.md"
    with jsonl.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for r in rows: f.write(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    fields = ["path","line","raw_mention","mention_family","nearby_dates","nearby_date_families","context"]
    with csvp.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fields); w.writeheader()
        for r in rows:
            rr = dict(r); rr["nearby_dates"] = "; ".join(rr["nearby_dates"]); rr["nearby_date_families"] = "; ".join(rr["nearby_date_families"]); w.writerow(rr)
    fams = Counter(r["mention_family"] for r in rows); files = Counter(r["path"] for r in rows)
    summary.write_text("\n".join([
        "# SAT Mention Extraction Test", "", f"Generated UTC: {now()}", f"Stopped reason: {stop}", f"Files scanned: {scanned}", f"Unreadable selected files: {unreadable}", f"Rows: {len(rows)}", "", "## Mention families", "", *[f"- {k}: {v}" for k,v in fams.most_common()], "", "## Top files", "", *[f"- {k}: {v}" for k,v in files.most_common(30)], "", "Outputs:", "- .[⚙️_AI_FILES]/TAGS/sat_mentions_test.jsonl", "- .[⚙️_AI_FILES]/TAGS/sat_mentions_test.csv", ""]), encoding="utf-8")
    (LOGS / f"tag_sat_mentions_test_{stamp()}.txt").write_text(f"SAT MENTION EXTRACTION TEST\nUTC: {now()}\nFILES_SCANNED: {scanned}\nROWS: {len(rows)}\nSTOPPED_REASON: {stop}\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"SAT mention extraction test complete: {len(rows)} rows from {scanned} files")

if __name__ == "__main__": main()

def bool_field(value: str | None, default: bool = False) -> bool:

def safe_repo_path(text: str) -> Path:

def ensure_parent(path: Path) -> None:

def copy_any(src: Path, dst: Path) -> str:
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not src.exists():
        return f"MISS source: {rel(src)}"
    if dst.exists():
        return f"SKIP destination exists: {rel(dst)}"
    if src.is_dir():
        shutil.copytree(src, dst)
        return f"COPY_TREE {rel(src)} -> {rel(dst)}"
    shutil.copy2(src, dst)

def request_has_real_tasks(text: str) -> bool:
    for raw_line in text.splitlines():

@dataclass
class TaskBlock:
    task: str
    fields: dict[str, str]
    text: str = ""


def parse_tasks(raw: str) -> list[TaskBlock]:
    lines = raw.splitlines()
    tasks: list[TaskBlock] = []
    current: TaskBlock | None = None
    collecting_text = False
    text_lines: list[str] = []

    def finish_current() -> None:
        nonlocal current, text_lines, collecting_text
        if current is not None:
            if text_lines:
                current.text = "\n".join(text_lines).rstrip()
            tasks.append(current)
        current = None
        text_lines = []
        collecting_text = False

    for raw_line in lines:
        line = raw_line.rstrip("\n")

        if collecting_text:
            if line.strip() == "ENDTEXT":
                collecting_text = False
                if current is not None:
                    current.text = "\n".join(text_lines).rstrip()
                text_lines = []
            else:
                text_lines.append(line)
            continue

        stripped = line.strip()
        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"):
            continue

        if stripped.upper().startswith("TASK:"):
            finish_current()
            current = TaskBlock(task=stripped.split(":", 1)[1].strip().upper(), fields={})
            continue

        if current is None:
            current = TaskBlock(task="LEGACY", fields={})

        if stripped.upper() == "TEXT:":
            collecting_text = True
            text_lines = []
            continue

        if ":" in stripped:
            k, v = stripped.split(":", 1)
            current.fields[k.strip().upper()] = v.strip()
        else:
            current.fields.setdefault("LINES", "")
            current.fields["LINES"] += stripped + "\n"

    finish_current()
    return tasks
